notes.about: Gujarati, in a script the engine has no rules of its own for: this file is all it knows. Sources: data/manifests/guwiki.json, guwikisource.json, guwikiquote.json, aksharantar-guj.json.
notes.notWord: The digits ૦-૯, the abbreviation sign ૰ and the rupee sign ૱.
notes.firstLetter: Independent vowels, consonants, ૐ, ૠ ૡ and ૹ. Never a sign, the anusvara, candrabindu or visarga.
notes.signs: Vowel signs and the virama must follow a consonant (or the nukta). ં ઁ ઃ are left out: they can follow an independent vowel (આં, અઃ).
notes.replace: ZWJ (U+200D) and ZWNJ (U+200C) are dropped; the engine's normal form drops them too, as there is no joiners field. The rest are the sequences the Unicode Standard's Gujarati section says not to use: an independent vowel typed as અ or આ plus a sign, and a two-part sign typed as its two halves, in either order (scanned books on Wikisource have તેા for તો 3,202 times); the sign rules come first, so અ + ે + ા also becomes ઓ.
notes.phraseBreaks: Gujarati ends sentences with Latin punctuation; the dandas are listed for verse.
